“Oral administration of glucocorticoids impairs absorption.”
“Glucocorticoids are metabolized by the kidneys.”

label: Medication/Risk factor/Manifestation question - Neupogen/Neulasta
stem: The nurse is teaching a client with osteosarcoma who has a new prescription for Filgrastim. Which of the following information should the nurse include?
options: “Filgrastim is taken before chemotherapy treatments.”
“Neutropenia is a risk factor for taking Filgrastim.”
“Bone pain is an adverse effect of Filgrastim use.”
“Kostmann syndrome is a risk factor for Filgrastim.”

label: Teaching question - Antibiotic (doxycycline)
stem: The nurse is teaching a client who has a new prescription for doxycycline. Which of the following statements by the client would indicate a correct understanding of the teaching?
options: “I can expect to experience yellowing of the skin and eyes while taking the medication.”
“I should take the medication with a glass of milk before bed.”
“I will discontinue the medication when I have a temperature less than 101°F (38.3°C).”
“I need to limit my sun exposure while taking the medication.”

label: Priority
stem: The nurse has received information about assigned clients. The nurse should first assess the client with
options: peptic ulcer disease who is reporting stool with a coffee-ground appearance
diabetes mellitus who is scheduled to receive metformin now
heart failure and 2+ peripheral edema who is currently eating lunch
bacterial pneumonia who is disoriented and diaphoretic

label: Priority
stem: The nurse in the emergency department has collected information about clients waiting to be seen. The nurse should first assess the client who has
options: epistaxis and takes aspirin
dysuria and takes tamsulosin
vomiting and reports frequent loose stools
persistent cough and reports night sweats

label: Priority
stem: The nurse is caring for assigned clients. The nurse should first assess the client who
options: has pneumonia and a temperature of 100 F (37.8 C)
has cellulitis of the right lower leg and a heart rate of 130/min
has ulcerative colitis and severe abdominal cramping
has a history of a stroke and is unable to lift the arm on the affected side

label: Priority
stem: The nurse is caring for assigned clients. The nurse should first assess the client who has
options: decreased bowel sounds and reports yellowish-green emesis
jaundice of the sclerae and reports a moderate level of anxiety
abdominal cramping and reports 3 black stools in the past 24 hours
an elevated lipase level and reports upper abdominal pain rated as 9 on a scale of 0-10

label: Priority
stem: The nurse is triaging clients at the site of a mass casualty event. The nurse should ensure that the first client transported to the hospital is the client who has
options: a cervical spine fracture and fixed pupils
an abrasion to the left leg and warm left foot
a closed fracture of the right arm and bruising of the right hand
an incomplete amputation of the left forearm and a palpable radial pulse

label: Intervene
stem: The nurse is observing staff members caring for a client during a surgical procedure. Which of the following actions by a staff member would require the nurse to intervene?
options: The surgeon wipes sweat from the forehead and continues operating
The anesthesia provider completes a time out before administering general anesthesia
The unlicensed assistive personnel counts sponges before suturing begins
The circulating nurse provides updates to family members throughout the procedure

label: Priority
stem: The nurse is caring for a client who is receiving mechanical ventilation. The nurse notes the low pressure alarm is sounding. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
options: Suction the client’s airway
Administer an anxiolytic medication to the client
Check the ventilator tubing for a leak
Observe for condensation in the ventilator tubing

label: Intervene
stem: The nurse is observing a staff member perform a central venous access device dressing change. The nurse should intervene if the staff member is observed
options: cleansing the insertion site with alcohol for 10 seconds using friction
allowing the insertion site to air dry completely before applying the new dressing
placing a surgical mask on the client and applying clean gloves before removing the old dressing
applying a CHG patch over the insertion site and covering it with a sterile transparent dressing

label: Priority
stem: The nurse is caring for a client who has a do not attempt resuscitation (DNAR) directive and experiences sudden cardiac arrest. The client’s spouse states, “Do something!” Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Ask security personnel to escort the client's spouse out of the room
Explain the DNAR directive to the client’s spouse
Begin chest compressions for the client
Notify the client’s health care provider

label: Teaching
stem: The nurse is teaching a staff education program about client confidentiality. Which of the following should the nurse include as an example of a violation of client confidentiality?
options: faxing information from a client’s medical record to the receiving facility prior to transferring a client
discussing a client’s condition with the health care provider in the cafeteria
texting a client’s health care provider using a secured messaging service
discussing a client’s plan of care during a change-of-shift report

label: Priority question - Chest Tube
stem: The nurse is assessing a client who has a chest tube attached to a closed-chest drainage system. Which of the following findings would be a priority to follow up?
options: serous drainage in the collection chamber
crepitus around the insertion site
intermittent bubbling in the water-seal chamber
clamped drainage tubing

label: Intervene question - Pneumonia
stem: The nurse is assessing a client who has bacterial pneumonia. Which of the following findings would be a priority to follow up?
options: headache and fever
sore throat and nasal congestion
use of accessory muscles
purulent sputum

label: Plan of care question - COPD
stem: The nurse is planning care for a client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Which of the following interventions should the nurse include in the client's plan of care? Select all that apply.
options: Recommend that the client sleep in the supine position.
Tell the client to eat 2 to 3 large meals each day.
Encourage the client to receive the influenza vaccine annually.
Demonstrate the huff-cough technique for the client.
Instruct the client to limit physical activity.

label: Manifestations question - Cystic fibrosis
stem: The nurse has attended a staff education program about cystic fibrosis. Which of the following should the nurse recognize as a complication of cystic fibrosis? Select all that apply.
options: malnutrition
osteoporosis
uterine fibroids
diabetes mellitus
portal hypertension

label: Teaching question - Asthma
stem: The nurse has taught a client with newly diagnosed asthma. Which of the following statements by the client would require follow-up? Select all that apply.
options: “I should take ibuprofen if I experience a headache.”
“I will measure my peak expiratory flow rate daily.”
“I should avoid exercising to decrease my symptoms.”
“I will wash my bedsheets in warm water weekly.”
“I should avoid taking inhaled corticosteroids during an acute exacerbation.”

label: Priority question - Asthma attack- Calee
stem: The nurse is assessing a client who is experiencing an acute exacerbation of asthma. Which of the following findings would require immediate follow-up?
options: abrupt discontinuation of wheezing
use of accessory muscles
nonproductive cough
difficulty speaking

label: Intervene question - Hyperoxygenation of COPD client (Valerie)
stem: The nurse is observing a staff member caring for a client with COPD. The nurse should intervene if the staff member is observed
options: demonstrating pursed-lip breathing for the client
providing the client with information about smoking cessation
administering albuterol to the client before meals
hyperoxygenating the client before assisting the client to ambulate

label: Plan of care question - Chest tube (Andrew)
stem: The nurse is caring for a client who has a chest tube attached to a closed-chest drainage system. Which of the following actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.
options: Avoid stripping or milking the client’s chest tube.
Clamp the chest tube while the client is ambulating.
Withhold analgesics to prevent respiratory depression.
Monitor the insertion site for subcutaneous emphysema.
Instruct the client to avoid coughing and deep breathing.

label: Medication/Risk factor/Manifestation question - (Megan)
stem: The nurse is caring for a client who is experiencing an acute exacerbation of asthma. The nurse should prepare to administer
options: albuterol
salmeterol
fluticasone
montelukast

label: Teaching question - Pediatric inhaler teaching with spacer (Holly B.)
stem: The nurse has taught the parent of a 6-year-old client with asthma who has a new prescription for an albuterol metered dose inhaler (MDI). Which of the following statements by the parent would indicate a correct understanding of the teaching? Select all that apply.
options: “I should wait 30 seconds before administering a second puff of medication to my child.”
“My child should hold the breath for 5 to 10 seconds after each puff of medication.”
“My child should inhale quickly after each puff to fully take in the medication.”
“A spacer will help my child effectively receive the medication.”
“I should shake the MDI before attaching it to a spacer.”

label: Question
stem: The nurse is assessing a client with pyelonephritis. Which of the following findings would be consistent with the condition? Select all that apply .
options: fever
dysuria
nausea
flank pain
periorbital edema

label: Question
stem: The nurse is planning care for a client who is receiving mechanical ventilation. Which of the following interventions should the nurse include in the client's plan of care? Select all that apply .
options: Perform oral care for the client once daily
Maintain the head of the client’s bed at less than 30 degrees
Hyperoxygenate the client with 100% oxygen before suctioning
Apply a sequential compression device to the client’s lower extremities
Perform endotracheal suctioning only when the high-pressure alarm sounds

label: Question
stem: The nurse is teaching the parents of school-age children about the treatment of pediculosis capitis (head lice). Which of the following information should the nurse include? Select all that apply .
options: “Wash your child’s bed linens in cold water.”
“Keep your child’s fingernails trimmed short.”
“Remove nits from your child’s head using a fine-tooth comb.”
“Treat all your household pets with a pediculicide.”
“Seal non-washable items in a plastic bag for 10 to 14 days.”

label: Question
stem: The nurse is planning care for a client with cellulitis of the right foot. Which of the following interventions should the nurse include in the client’s plan of care? Select all that apply .
options: Put on a protective gown and clean gloves before entering the client’s room
Maintain the client’s affected extremity in a dependent position
Mark and date the area of inflammation
Apply warm compresses to the affected area
Encourage the client to ambulate frequently

label: Question
stem: The nurse is planning a staff education program about syphilis. Which of the following information should the nurse include? Select all that apply .
options: “All clients should be tested for syphilis during pregnancy.”
“Antibiotics should be prescribed for syphilis even if the initial chance has healed.”
“Syphilis can affect the brain, eyes, ears, and other organs.”
“Syphilis increases the risk of contracting HIV and other sexually-transmitted infections.”
“Cesarean birth helps protect newborns from contracting syphilis.”

label: Question
stem: The nurse is screening clients for trichomoniasis. Which of the following findings would be consistent with trichomoniasis? Select all that apply .
options: frothy, yellow-green vaginal discharge
vesicular lesions around the genitals
itching and inflammation of the vulva
pain with sexual intercourse
foul-smelling penile discharge

label: Question
stem: The nurse is teaching a client who has pubic lice. Which of the following information should the nurse include? Select all that apply .
options: Wash and dry your linens using hot water and high heat.
Use a pediculicide product to kill the lice.
Follow the product instructions for repeating the treatment.
Check your pets in the home for lice.
Notify your recent sexual partners about the risk of infestation.
Soak your hair brushes and accessories in hot water.

label: Question
stem: The nurse is talking with a female client who has human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and genital warts. Which of the following statements by the client would require follow-up? Select all that apply .
options: My sexual partners may have HPV infection even if they are not experiencing symptoms.
I will be immune to genital warts in the future after these warts are removed.
The HPV vaccine is not effective after HPV infection has already occurred.
I should schedule routine Pap tests to monitor for cervical changes.
Cervical cancer is the only cancer related to HPV infection.

label: Question
stem: The nurse is caring for a client who had a right-sided stroke. Which of the following complications is the client at risk for developing? Select all that apply .
options: aspiration
joint contractures
impulsive behavior
numbness of the feet
impaired concept of time

label: Question
stem: The nurse has taught a client who is entering the 3rd trimester of pregnancy. Which of the following statements would indicate a correct understanding of the teaching? Select all that apply .
options: Fetal movement is expected to decrease toward the end of the pregnancy.
Lightening makes it easier to breathe but can cause increased bladder pressure.
Spontaneous rupture of membranes can cause a large gush or slow trickle of fluid.
True labor occurs when regular contractions cause progressive dilation of the cervix.
Blurry vision and a severe headache are common discomforts of pregnancy.
